newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEES, ASLK DEALS COULD TRIGGER CAP INCREASE - FORTIS.
newsitem.headline: MEES, ASLK DEALS COULD TRIGGER CAP INCREASE - FORTIS.

text.p: Belgo-Dutch bancassurance group said it might have to increase its capital to finance the purchase of Dutch investment bank MeesPierson and additional shares in Belgian bank ASLK/CGER.

"If the two operations go through -- something we absolutely do not yet know at the moment -- it is possible that we will go for a capital increase," Fortis co-chairman Maurice Lippens told Belgian newspaper De Standaard in an interview published on Wednesday.
Fortis is negotiating the sale of MeesPierson with Dutch banking group ABN AMRO. Analysts say the deal could cost Fortis up to 2.5 billion guilders.
ASLK-CGER was partially privatised three years ago with the sale of 49.9 percent of the bank to Fortis.

The bank recently received A+ long-term and short-term A1 ratings from European credit ratings agency IBCA, which said the bank's performance had improved steadily since its privatisation as income had risen and costs had been reduced.
It said the bank's strength lay in its market share which was 20 percent for customer funding, which easily exceeds its customer lending.
Lippens said Fortis remained interested in raising its stake in ASLK, but it was not yet clear how the Belgian government would handle the reduction of its holdings.
"We expect the government to exercise its put option on 9.8 percent of the shares next year or sell another 15 percent. Or do both," he said. "In any case we would like to purchase further shares."

Lippens said Fortis had an open mind on the issue of listing ASLK shares on the bourse, but warned any offering should ensure that investors would not be disappointed as had been the case in the listing of privatised Belgian gas distributor Distrigas SA.
Shares in Distrigas, sold to investors at 28,000 francs in June, were trading at 25,250 francs on the Brussels bourse on Wednesday.
"To make sure, one would have to allow a discount on the intrinsic value of the share," he noted.
A second problem was that ASLK actually comprised two companies: ASLK Bank and ASLK Insurance. "You cannot take both to the market," Lippens said.
Fortis is due to publish nine-months results on Thursday.
Analysts expect it to announce a net profit rise of just over 17 percent to 549 million Ecus, a slower rise when compared to the first half increase of 21 percent to 366 million Ecus.
That rise was mainly driven by the group's banking business where profits rose by 27 percent to 258 million Ecus.
The final quarter of the year is expected to make up for the slow-down in growth.
Analysts are upbeat on the purchase of MeesPierson, which should be completed before the end of the year.
